incidents.title: Payment API returning 500 errors
incidents.description: Production Payment Service is throwing consecutive HTTP 500 errors on the /v1/charges and /v1/checkout endpoints. Connection pool timeouts observed following recent release.
incidents.impactSummary: Checkout failures impacting ~14.8% of global customer credit card transactions via Stripe/Adyen endpoints. Elevated cart abandonments reported in US-East.

incidents.title: API Gateway rate limiter thread lock under flash traffic
incidents.description: A flash sale event triggered Redis token-bucket locking in edge gateway worker pools, causing 429 Too Many Requests to be served incorrectly to non-throttled callers.
incidents.impactSummary: Approximately 5% of web requests intermittently receiving false 429 throttles for 12 minutes.

incidents.title: Order Service Kafka consumer lag exceeding 45,000 messages
incidents.description: Partition 3 consumer group on topic `orders.finalized` stalled due to a deserialization failure with a malformed promo code payload.
incidents.impactSummary: Order confirmation emails and downstream analytics delayed by ~8 minutes; order placement unaffected.

incidents.title: Database Service read replica replication lag > 180s in eu-central-1
incidents.description: Cross-region physical replication streaming broke after an AWS network partition, causing read replica to fall behind WAL timeline.
incidents.impactSummary: European users observing slightly stale balance display until replication catches up.

incidents.title: Notification Service FCM token refresh rate limit exceeded
incidents.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging client credentials triggered Google API quota limits for Android push notifications.
incidents.impactSummary: Android push notifications delayed by up to 25 minutes; fallback SMS active.

incidents.title: User Service Redis session cache eviction causing slow auth checks
incidents.description: Maxmemory policy was set to noeviction on redis-auth-01, resulting in OOM on new session key creation.
incidents.impactSummary: Users experienced momentary login re-prompting during memory pressure; resolved by switching eviction policy to volatile-lru.

incidents.title: Payment Service 3D-Secure 2.0 challenge iframe failure on Safari 17.4
incidents.description: Strict Content-Security-Policy header blocked redirect postmessage from Visa Secure verified domain.
incidents.impactSummary: EU customers using Safari unable to complete card authentication step for 58 minutes.

incidents.title: Database Service autovacuum freeze job consuming 98% disk IOPS
incidents.description: Transaction ID wraparound prevention triggered aggressive autovacuum during unexpected midday order rush.
incidents.impactSummary: Database latency elevated by 60ms; autovacuum throttled via vacuum_cost_limit.

incidents.title: Order Service duplicate idempotency key evaluation failure
incidents.description: Concurrency race in the distributed lock manager allowed two rapid clicks on Submit Order to generate duplicate records.
incidents.impactSummary: Found 3 duplicate test orders; DB unique constraint caught payments correctly.

incidents.title: Notification Service webhook signature verification drift
incidents.description: Clock skew between notification worker nodes caused webhook HMAC sha256 timestamps to fail verification by 12 seconds.
incidents.impactSummary: Confined to staging environment. NTP daemon resynchronized.

evidence.content:
Commit: 8f9b1c2 "feat(payments): Introduce automated fraud risk assessment v2 with DB schema migration"
Author: dev-deployer-bot

evidence.title: Root Cause Hypothesis & War Room Summary
evidence.content: Root cause confirmed: Migration V482 took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the core `transactions` table. Because of continuous traffic, all write queries backed up in the Hikari pool until it reached the 200 connection ceiling. We are executing an emergency kill of the blocking migration query and temporarily increasing the pool size while rollback is finalized.

hypotheses.title: Database connection pool exhaustion
hypotheses.description: HikariCP client connection pool reached the maximum 200 connection ceiling, causing all incoming API requests on /v1/charges to time out after 30,000ms while waiting for an available database socket.
supportingEvidence: DB connections reached 100% capacity (Aurora PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity reports 198 of 200 connections active in wait_event: Lock:tuple)
Connection acquisition timeout failures escalated in HikariPool-1 (requests timing out after 30,005ms)
API latency increased dramatically (P99 latency surged from 145ms baseline to 4,820ms)
HTTP 500 errors surged to 182 req/sec (error rate reaching 14.82% vs 0.50% threshold)
contradictingEvidence: No direct database infrastructure redeployment or parameter group modification occurred during the outage window
hypotheses.conclusion: This is a strong hypothesis but requires human verification.
recommendedSteps: Query pg_stat_activity filtered by state="active" and wait_event="Lock:tuple" to isolate thread contention
Inspect HikariCP connection leak detection logs and active pool thread dumps in Elasticsearch
Verify if database connection limits can be temporarily scaled via RDS Proxy or connection pooler

recommendedRunbooks.title: Payment Service HikariCP Emergency Pool Tuning
recommendedRunbooks.description: Temporarily increase max-pool-size to 350 to drain queued charge transactions.
recommendedRunbooks.command: kubectl set env deployment/payment-service HIKARI_MAX_POOL_SIZE=350 -n production

recommendedRunbooks.title: Audit Postgres Lock Graph & Blocked Transactions
recommendedRunbooks.description: Execute read-only lock graph query to locate the root blocking PID.
recommendedRunbooks.command: SELECT blocked_locks.pid AS blocked_pid, blocking_locks.pid AS blocking_pid, blocking_activity.query FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked_locks JOIN pg_catalog.pg_locks blocking_locks ON blocking_locks.locktype = blocked_locks.locktype AND blocking_locks.database IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.database AND blocking_locks.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.relation AND blocking_locks.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.page AND blocking_locks.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.tuple AND blocking_locks.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.virtualxid AND blocking_locks.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.transactionid AND blocking_locks.classid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.classid AND blocking_locks.objid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objid AND blocking_locks.objsubid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objsubid AND blocking_locks.pid != blocked_locks.pid JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocking_activity ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking_locks.pid;

hypotheses.title: Recent deployment correlation
hypotheses.description: Release v2.41.0-release was rolled out via ArgoCD 6 minutes prior to error rate escalation, applying database schema migration V482__add_fraud_v2.sql with an unbatched table alter.
supportingEvidence: Deployment occurred at 05:08:44Z shortly before the incident detection at 05:14:22Z
Deployment commit 8f9b1c2 introduced automated fraud risk evaluation v2 with a flyway DB schema migration
Checkout error rates and 500 error spikes emerged immediately after pod rollout finalized
contradictingEvidence: Staging pipeline smoke tests and initial canary verification passed prior to full production promotion
No CPU spike or OOM crash detected in the payment-service application containers themselves
hypotheses.conclusion: High temporal correlation; the migration script included in the deployment is the probable trigger for the secondary database lock contention.
recommendedSteps: Review git diff for commit 8f9b1c2 and flyway migration script V482__add_fraud_v2.sql
Evaluate rollback viability for payment-service container image back to v2.40.9
Check if automated rollback can be initiated without schema incompatibility

recommendedRunbooks.title: Payment Service Immediate Rollback via ArgoCD
recommendedRunbooks.description: Rollback payment-service Helm release to previous stable revision v2.40.9.

hypotheses.title: Long-running database transactions & lock contention
hypotheses.description: An exclusive table lock held by an ALTER TABLE query on the `transactions` table caused all subsequent transactional writes to queue up indefinitely, blocking worker connections.
supportingEvidence: Aurora PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity reveals migration script #482 executing ALTER TABLE transactions ADD COLUMN risk_evaluation_v2 JSONB (locked table for 8.4 mins)
198 active connections are blocked waiting on wait_event: Lock:tuple
Transaction timeout errors in logs indicate client threads blocked waiting on row locks
contradictingEvidence: Primary database host CPU utilization is nominal at 42%, and IOPS is below provisioned burst limits, indicating logical locking rather than hardware resource exhaustion
hypotheses.conclusion: Explains why connection pool saturated without infrastructure CPU or memory exhaustion. Resolving the blocking DDL transaction should release queued worker threads.
recommendedSteps: Identify the exact Postgres backend PID executing the migration script using pg_stat_activity
Verify whether cancelling the blocking query releases table locks immediately
Check transactions table size and plan off-peak zero-downtime migration using pg_repack or pt-online-schema-change equivalent

recommendedRunbooks.title: Emergency Terminate Blocking Database Session
recommendedRunbooks.description: Safely terminate the blocking migration PID holding the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on transactions table.
recommendedRunbooks.command: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state="active" AND query LIKE "%ALTER TABLE transactions%" AND pid != pg_backend_pid();

recommendedInvestigationSteps: Terminate blocking migration query via pg_terminate_backend(pid) on db-prod-main
Monitor HikariCP active connection pool drain and error rates on /v1/charges
If error rate remains elevated after lock release, execute immediate rollback of deployment v2.41.0-release
Post-mitigation: rewrite schema migration with zero-downtime DDL (ADD COLUMN DEFAULT NULL or pg_repack)

recommendedRunbooks.title: Emergency: Terminate Blocking Migration Transaction
recommendedRunbooks.description: Terminates the specific backend holding the exclusive lock on `transactions` table.
recommendedRunbooks.command: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE "%ALTER TABLE transactions%" AND pid != pg_backend_pid();

recommendedRunbooks.title: Emergency: Temporary HikariCP Pool Expansion
recommendedRunbooks.description: Expands connection pool limit from 200 to 350 to drain backlog once lock is freed.
recommendedRunbooks.command: kubectl set env deployment/payment-service HIKARI_MAX_POOL_SIZE=350 -n production
